title: Build a Pluggable Rate-Limiting Library
summary:
Build the library behind every API gateway's `429 Too Many Requests`. Two algorithms — a **token bucket** (bursty but bounded) and a **sliding-window counter** (the Cloudflare approximation that fixes the fixed-window boundary burst) — sit behind one **Strategy interface**, so a `RateLimiter` can stack rules like *10/s burst AND 1000/hour* and charge **all of them or none**. Everything runs on an **injected clock**, keys are **memory-bounded** (LRU cap + idle sweep), and every denial carries an exact `retryAfterMs` that becomes a `Retry-After` header.

Interview payoff: you can derive the sliding-window estimate and its retry time on a whiteboard, explain why a failed multi-rule check must not partially charge, and discuss what happens to limits when you evict state (fail-open) — and how this maps onto a Redis Lua script in a distributed deployment.

milestones.name: M1: Token bucket
milestones.description: Lazy continuous refill capped at capacity, `check` (no charge, no state) vs `consume` (charge only when allowed), exact `retryAfterMs`, `Infinity` for cost > capacity, `RangeError` on bad config/cost.

milestones.name: M2: Sliding-window counter
milestones.description: Current + previous fixed-window counts with `prev * (1 - elapsed/W) + curr`. No boundary burst. Exact `retryAfterMs` both inside the current window and when you must wait for the next one.

milestones.name: M3: Multi-rule limiter
milestones.description: `RateLimiter([...rules])`: allowed only if all allow, `remaining = min`, denied → `deniedBy` + `retryAfterMs = max`. A denied request charges no rule. `reset(key)` across rules.

milestones.name: M4: Memory bound
milestones.description: `maxKeys` evicts the least-recently-used key; `sweep()` drops keys that are indistinguishable from fresh (full bucket / empty windows).

milestones.name: M5: Retry-After
milestones.description: `retryAfterHeader(ms)` → whole seconds rounded up, `null` for never.
